tools_helpful.evidence: session-log.txt L209-215: bootstrap copied source, preserved .uwp-source, produced MIGRATION-MAPPING.md / MIGRATION-DEFERRED.md and namespace-rewrote files cleanly; build ultimately SUCCEEDED (build-output.txt).
Agent added a 'No camera device found on this machine.' fallback panel; score note credits it as an improvement that renders a non-blank frame (migration-score.json feature note).

tool_limitations.limitation: unsupported-api-inventory.json routes the media-capture family and CaptureElement to anchor 'capture', but MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md has no <a id="capture"> section, so the helper would exit 1 (anchor not found).
tool_limitations.suggested_tweak: Add a real 'capture' anchor section with the camera-preview recipe.

failed_apis.root_cause: CaptureElement does not exist in WinUI 3; the skill told the agent to DEFER it as having 'no compatible replacement'. In fact it migrates to an <Image> fed by MediaCapture preview frames via SoftwareBitmapSource.
failed_apis.fix: Replace <CaptureElement> with <Image>; new SoftwareBitmapSource; poll GetPreviewFrameAsync -> convert to Bgra8/Premultiplied -> SetBitmapAsync.

failed_apis.why_tried: UWP attaches a live FaceDetectionEffect to MediaCapture.
failed_apis.root_cause: CS0246 x22: the agent only had 'using Windows.Media.FaceAnalysis' (which holds FaceDetector, NOT FaceDetectionEffect); FaceDetectionEffect/FaceDetectedEventArgs live in Windows.Media.Core. Agent spent many turns speculating the namespace was unprojected / needed a NuGet package before pivoting.
failed_apis.fix: For the Image-based preview, run FaceDetector.DetectFacesAsync on each polled frame (convert to Gray8) instead of a live effect.

doc_errors.where: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md L53-55 '### CS0246 / WMC0001 CaptureElement' + unsupported-api-inventory.json 'unsupported' list
doc_errors.wrong: 'there is no compatible replacement' and 'mark the file defer'.
doc_errors.correct: CaptureElement DOES have a standard WinUI 3 migration: <Image> + SoftwareBitmapSource fed by MediaCapture GetPreviewFrameAsync / MediaFrameReader frames. Deferring a camera page leaves a blank window and loses the whole feature.

special_apis.special_handling: requires Bgra8 + Premultiplied; convert with SoftwareBitmap.Convert before SetBitmapAsync.
requires Gray8 bitmap; FaceDetector.CreateAsync() then DetectFacesAsync(gray8).

errors_encountered.error: Xaml Internal Error WMC9999: Object reference not set to an instance of an object (+ WMC1509)
errors_encountered.root_cause: XAML referenced {ThemeResource SystemErrorTextColor}, a UWP theme key that does not exist in WinUI 3. A dangling resource key crashes the XAML markup compiler opaquely instead of emitting a clear 'resource not found'. Agent first blamed FaceDetectionEffect for the crash, wasting turns.
errors_encountered.fix: removed/replaced the invalid theme-resource key with a valid Fluent brush.

dev_agent_struggles.where: MainPage.xaml.cs face detection + MainPage.xaml theme brush
dev_agent_struggles.symptom: cascading CS0246 + opaque WMC9999 XAML compiler crash; agent looped between 'namespace not projected / add NuGet' and 'clean build cache' theories.
dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: many turns of speculation (build-events.jsonl CS0246 reasoning blocks)
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: two independent defects conflated: (1) FaceDetectionEffect wrong namespace, (2) invalid theme-resource key crashing markup compiler.
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: pivoted FaceDetectionEffect->FaceDetector and removed the bad theme key.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: skill section that (a) gives the CaptureElement->Image+SoftwareBitmapSource recipe and pairs FaceDetectionEffect->FaceDetector on frames, and (b) warns that unknown UWP System* theme keys crash the XAML compiler with WMC9999 rather than a clear error.

env_issues.issue: No camera device on the VM; all three buttons stay IsEnabled=False so behavior cannot be actuated.
env_issues.workaround: defensive fallback panel keeps the frame non-blank; score capped at partial (50) for unverifiable behavior, no regression vs UWP.
